openings.claim: A conventional paired-results review with targeted label adjudication can support a reproducible advance, reject or unresolved decision while identifying affected slices and accounting for every adjudication.
openings.delta: Change the decision dependency from provisional labels alone to a paired gain table backed by selected sealed adjudications. Rank flagged rows by whether their possible supplied labels could change the overall or slice acceptance result; break ties by record identifier. The carrier is a spreadsheet or local script plus sampling log.
openings.prediction: Compared with the nearest rival, a balanced slice-quota audit with deterministic identifier ordering, targeted review may resolve more threshold-relevant uncertainty per adjudication. Differing observations would be remaining decision uncertainty and adjudications consumed, checked against the sealed full-label key. Equal results, or a rival-supported decision when targeted review remains unresolved, defeat that advantage; neither outcome is stipulated.
openings.probe: On matched copies, run targeted review and the rival with independently reset sixteen-row allowances and seventy-minute limits. Select withholding rows before both runs. Recompute paired gain and slice bounds after each accessible adjudication, using only labels supported by supplied records. Log selection reasons, returned labels, unavailable attempts and time; unavailable attempts consume no adjudication allowance. Advance only when every remaining permissible label completion meets gain >=4 and each slice loss <=2; reject only when no completion meets both; otherwise report unresolved. Freeze reports before opening the full-label key and compare decision support, slice accounting and log completeness.
assumptions: The supplied label vocabulary and flagged identifiers permit reproducible completion bounds within the available environment and time.

Informative accessible rows exist: flags with identical baseline and candidate predictions cannot change comparative gain. Withholding, remaining flags or computational limits may prevent certification.
No deployment conclusion follows; the probe evaluates a further-evaluation decision only.

assessment: Viable ordinary incumbent candidate; comparative advantage and decision feasibility remain uncertain until the bounded probe. Resource exhaustion alone supplies no evidence of success.
